links.outcome: Differences between development and Taiwanese validation cohort demographics, predictors, and outcome incidence
links.effect: Validation cohort differed in demographics, medicolegal and cultural context and key predictors; sustained opioid use incidence was 9.9% (270/2737) in development vs 3.3% (34/1037) in Taiwan (p < .01).
links.quote: Comparing the validation cohort to the developmental revealed significant differences in demographic profiles, medicolegal frameworks, ethnic cultural contexts and key predictors of postoperative opioid use identified by the SORG-MLA.

links.outcome: Calibration of SORG-MLA in the Taiwanese cohort
links.effect: Calibration curves showed the model overestimated risk of prolonged opioid use; recalibration with contemporary data recommended, though AUROC was 0.78 and AUPRC 0.35.
links.quote: Calibration curves indicated that the model overestimated the risk of prolonged opioid use.

links.outcome: Performance of SORG-MLA when applied to a new country population
links.effect: Discrimination was good (AUROC 0.78, AUPRC 0.35) and Brier 0.033 vs null 0.040, but risk was overestimated, indicating incomplete generalization.
links.quote: The model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an AUROC of 0.78 and an AUPRC of 0.35.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation study of an existing predictive algorithm (SORG-MLA) in an international cohort, evaluating model performance without testing specific deployment practices.
